why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: The words describe ordinary RNA-seq, but the libraries are QIAseq miRNA, size-selected to about 22 nt, and every metadata field says so; smrnaseq is the pipeline that reads them and gives mature-miRNA counts, which the reply should say is the only expression these reads hold. rnaseq is the lookalike and must not be offered: on these reads it would quantify almost nothing. riboseq is for footprints. rnasplice/smrnaseq-style required values: smrnaseq's mirtrace_species is a required user param that configure_run refuses without, so the story scripts the user's answer (hsa); the launch must carry hsa and the QIAseq 3' adapter AACTGTAGGCACCATCAAT, which the ExpressionKit field determines (the Illumina default would trim nothing).

ruling.note: Ruled by an independent Fable reviewer agent on the owner's instruction (2026-10-26). The metadata is unambiguous (miRNA-Seq, QIAseq kit, size fractionation), and smrnaseq gives the expression these reads hold, so a careful analyst says the libraries are small RNA and offers smrnaseq rather than asking; asking first is still allowed. Same launch requirements as the other smrnaseq stories.
